compliant

kum-PLY-unt -- three syllables, stress on the second syllable, PLY. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone or something compliant follows rules and requests as they are given -- a compliant person goes along willingly, and a compliant company or machine meets every rule that applies to it.

The airline kept its fleet compliant with every new inspection rule the agency issued.

Example

The moment the new dress code is posted, one compliant student reads it top to bottom, replaces his sneakers, tucks in his shirt, and shows up the next morning meeting every line of it.

Compliant means inclined to obey the rules as written, promptly and completely -- a readiness to follow requests, rules, and regulations.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

dutiful: Dutiful means careful to fulfill your obligations -- the dutiful son calls home every Sunday because he feels he owes it. Compliant is cooler and more procedural: a compliant person or company follows the rules and requests as written, with no felt sense of duty required.

cooperative: Cooperative describes willingly working together -- pitching in, sharing the load, meeting others halfway. Compliant is narrower and runs one way: a compliant firm or device follows the rules handed down to it, whether or not any teamwork is involved.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

rebellious: resisting authority or control

obstinate: stubbornly refusing to change or obey

Where it sits · what kind of authority gets followed

amenable → compliant → obedient

amenable vs. compliant: Amenable is warmer and looser than compliant: an amenable coworker is open to your suggestions, while a compliant one follows the posted procedure whether or not anyone is watching.

obedient vs. compliant: Obedient answers to a stronger authority than compliant does: a compliant contractor satisfies the written building code, while an obedient recruit does whatever the sergeant commands, the moment the order comes.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — com-: together, fully (Latin)

root — pli: to fill, to fulfill (from Latin plere, via complere 'to complete'; the same root spelled -ple- in complete)

suffix — -ant: in a state of; doing (Latin -antem)

Put it together: Compliant traces back to Latin complere, 'to fill up, to fulfill' -- com- ('fully') plus plere ('to fill'), spelled pli here -- drifting through Spanish and Italian as 'to fulfill what courtesy requires.' To be compliant is to fulfill what is asked of you: the request is made, and you fill it.

Use the root in a new word: complete: She stayed late to complete the last section of the application.

Word Building

Word Choice

Compliant is the language of rules and standards: compliant with regulations, a compliant device, a compliant taxpayer. Applied to people it can tip toward criticism -- 'a compliant press' suggests reporters too ready to go along. Keep it procedural: rules and requests are what one is compliant with.
